findings.text: Floating pointer structure holds a four character signature plus a physical address of the configuration table, a length in paragraphs, a specification version, a checksum byte and five feature bytes where the first distinguishes standard versus configured and the second carries firmware interrupt mode indication. Configuration header holds a four character signature, total length, specification revision, checksum, vendor and product identity, optional vendor table pointer size and count, local interrupt controller address and reserved word.

Configuration entry type codes are small integers starting at zero for processor and continuing in order for bus, input output interrupt controller, interrupt source and local interrupt source. A separate high translation code sits near the top of the byte range.

Processor entry carries type, local interrupt identifier and version, flag byte, feature values and reserved words. Availability and boot processor are single bit flags. Family model and stepping are selected by nibble masks. Bus entry carries type, bus identifier and a six character type name.

Bus type names are short uppercase texts for EISA, ISA, INTERN, MCA, VL, PCI, PCMCIA, CBUS, CBUSII, FUTURE, MBI, MBII, MPI, MPSA, NUBUS, TC, VME and XPRESS. Usable input output interrupt controller is indicated by the least significant flag bit.

Input output interrupt controller entry carries type, identifier, version, flags and memory address. Interrupt source entry carries type, source kind, flags, source bus and line plus destination controller and line. Source kinds order maskable interrupt, nonmaskable interrupt, system management interrupt and external interrupt from zero to three. Polarity uses low two bits with default, active high, reserved and active low meanings and trigger uses next two bits with default, edge, reserved and level meanings, each with a mask. Broadcast destination uses all bits set in a byte.

Local interrupt source entry parallels interrupt source but names source bus identifier and destination local input. Vendor table header holds a four character signature, length, revision, checksum and identifier. Vendor signature text is underscore followed by OEM. Simplified bus enumeration orders ISA then EISA then PCI starting at one.

Hypervisor IO interrupt base equals hex FEC00000. Virtual trust levels equal zero for normal, one for secure and two for management. Secondary processor start uses default page attribute pattern hex 0007040600070406 and segment limit hex FFFFFFFF.

General hypercall helper accepts a control value plus optional guest input and output buffers, substitutes zero physical address for absent buffers, invokes the hypervisor and returns status. Wide build dispatches through indirect static call, narrow build splits addresses into halves and reports all ones when no hypercall page is mapped.

Fast hypercall helpers combine a sixteen bit code with a fast indicator to form control, then forward one or two register carried values without memory buffers and return status. Wide builds use indirect static dispatch while narrow builds split values for an indirect call to the hypercall page.

Per processor assist accessor returns the stored assist page for the requested processor or null when the table is absent, with a fallback variant that always returns null. Fallback guest flush helpers report failure, MSR setters discard input while getters return zero, and identifier to virtual processor translation reports invalid argument.

Synthetic interrupt controller membership checks whether a register lies in the control through last channel interval, while channel membership checks first through last channel. Raw register read delegates to native read. Nonmaskable reason helper constantly returns zero in this configuration.

Many hypervisor and trust level helpers are empty or constant here: interrupt initialization, memory virtualization setup, crash setup, platform and early setup, timestamp callback management, guest communication termination, isolated register access and trust level return operations do nothing, while negotiation reports false and early and secure boot paths report success.
Flush list filler is a function pointer type returning integer status. Message interrupt allocation info aliases generic interrupt allocation info. Each header defines a unique inclusion guard macro.

Trust level processor context exposes general state both as named accumulator, counter, data, base, fault address, base pointer, source, destination and extended registers eight through fifteen and as an array of sixteen, followed by floating and vector state.

Message interrupt data word packs vector, delivery mode, logical destination indication, reserved bits, active level polarity and trigger mode, sharing storage with a remapping subhandle for alternate interpretation, using packed layout and an architecture alias.

Low message address packs destination mode, redirect hint, virtual and physical destination identifier portions and high base bits, with an alternate remapping interpretation carrying index, format and validity fields. High address carries upper destination identifier with reserved low byte. Low base constant reflects upper bits of the standard local interrupt range and high base constant is zero, both with architecture aliases and packed layout.
Supported vector message interrupt flags combine the generic mask with MSI-X and dynamic allocation capabilities, while required flags demand default domain and chip operations.

Architectural register numbers are hex C0000080 for extended features, C0000081 through C0000084 for legacy and long and compat call targets plus call mask, and C0000100 through C0000103 for FS base, GS base, kernel GS base and auxiliary timestamp.

Extended feature enable positions assign zero to call support, eight to long enable, ten to long active read only, eleven to no execute, twelve to virtualization, thirteen to segment limit, fourteen to fast save restore, fifteen to translation cache extensions and twenty one to automatic branch control, each with a single bit mask.
Memory type encodings assign zero to uncacheable, one to write combining, four to write through, five to write protected, six to write back and seven to weak uncacheable for attribute table only.

Flexible event delivery registers occupy hex 1CC through 1CF for ring stack pointers, 1D0 for exception levels, 1D1 through 1D3 for upper shadow stacks and 1D4 for configuration, with level zero shadow aliasing the privilege zero shadow pointer.

Test control register is at hex 33 with split lock detection at bit 29. Speculation control register is at hex 48 with bits for branch restriction, single thread predictor, store bypass disable, return speculation disable and branch history disable. Mitigations mask combines those five controls.

Prediction, inventory, performance, bus, platform and user wait registers use hex 49, 4E, 4F, C1, C2, CD, CE and E1. Prediction barriers sit at bits zero and seven. Platform info carries CPUID fault at bit 31. User wait control carries low power disable at bit zero and reserved at bit one, with time field preserving all but the low two bits.

Core capabilities register at hex CF reports integrity at bit two and split lock detection at bit five. Package sleep register at hex E2 uses high bits for automatic demotion and undemotion. Range register capability is at hex FE. Architecture capabilities register at hex 10A reports speculation and side channel properties in bits zero through eight and thirteen through nineteen, covering meltdown immunity, enhanced branch support, alternate predictors, entry flush skipping, store bypass and sampling immunity, code size change immunity, transaction control availability, async abort immunity, stale data variants, microcode enumeration, fill buffer clearing and controls, and return predictor scope.

Multiprocessor discovery relies on fixed signatures and on checksum bytes that bring the unsigned byte sum to zero, with lengths expressing structure size and unused and reserved fields expected to be zero.

Callers must handle absent hypervisor support: narrow hypercall without mapped page yields all ones, assist accessor may return null, fallback flush and translation helpers signal failure, and MSR getters return zero while setters ignore input.
External static call helper referenced by wide hypercall dispatch is owned elsewhere.
Alternate external static call helper referenced by hypercall handling is owned elsewhere.
External low half extractor referenced by narrow hypercall address splitting is owned elsewhere.
External high half extractor referenced by narrow hypercall address splitting is owned elsewhere.
